title: Explain the CIA Triad
description: Write a short security brief explaining the CIA triad to a non‑technical manager.
problemStatement:
## Scenario
You are a new cloud security analyst. Your team has been asked to give a 2‑minute overview of the CIA triad to the marketing department so they understand why security matters.

### Your Task
Write a **brief email** (100‑150 words) that:
- Defines Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability in simple, non‑technical language.
- Gives one concrete example for each pillar from everyday life (not just cloud).
- Ends with one sentence on why the CIA triad is the foundation of the company’s security strategy.
hints: Think of confidentiality as a locked diary, integrity as a tamper‑proof seal, availability as a 24/7 store.
Connect each pillar to something the marketing team cares about (customer data, campaign files, website uptime).
expectedOutput: Your brief should include clear definitions of all three pillars with examples, and a closing sentence linking them to business trust.
solutionCode:
Subject: The ABCs of Security – CIA Triad

Hi Marketing Team,

Every security decision we make is guided by three simple principles:

1. Confidentiality – Keeping secrets secret. Like a diary with a lock, we ensure only authorised people see sensitive data, such as customer addresses.
2. Integrity – Keeping data accurate. Think of a sealed envelope; if the seal is broken, you know it was tampered. We use checks to make sure campaign files aren’t altered by mistake or malice.
3. Availability – Keeping services running. Just as you expect a store to be open during business hours, our website must always be reachable for customers.

Together, these three pillars protect our reputation and earn customer trust. Every security tool we use, from firewalls to backups, ultimately supports the CIA triad.

Best,
[Your Name]
